claims.text: Paraguay Culture account; MJP French edition Restricted participation

Paraguay’s Culture account identifies Buenos Aires as former vice-regal capital and Asunción’s 1811 government choice. MJP’s French edition locates the separate United Provinces declaration at Tucumán in 1816. Shared administration did not make one declaration; the account explicitly describes restricted participation.
Did the former vice-regal centre make the two later acts one Buenos Aires declaration? Different actors and acts: Asunción 1811 and Tucumán 1816

claims.text: Why cannot the 1816 Tucumán declaration stand for the 1811 Asunción choice? They are distinct dated actions by different political bodies; the earlier shared vice-regal relation does not merge them.

The shared vice-regal relation does not merge the 1811 Asunción government choice and 1816 Tucumán declaration. Restricted participation remains explicit; no universal representation or Indigenous consent follows.
